clue.text: Wasps of a kind, see, reverse of troublesome?

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its last letter back to its first
the word is taken for its sound alone, which matches the name of a single letter

blocks.note: the letter C is pronounced like this word
a spiny problem is a thorny, troublesome one

explanation.surface: A naturalist points out a type of wasp that is the opposite of a pest.
explanation.walkthrough: CYNIPS is the gall-wasp genus; the question mark admits that a letter standing for its spoken name is a liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynips is the genus of gall wasps, so the name covers one particular kind of wasp.

clue.text: Endless sign of problem with engines arising — before they do?

definitions.text: Endless sign of problem with engines arising — before they do?

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter
in a down clue, rising means reading from the bottom upward

blocks.note: engine knock is the rattling sound of faulty combustion

explanation.surface: A mechanic notes that engines start knocking just before they break down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: KNOCK, trimmed and turned up, gives CONK, and engines knock before they conk (out), that is, fail.
explanation.definitionFit: To conk, or conk out, is colloquial for an engine breaking down, which knocking often heralds.

clue.text: Dreamy music, not once preceding payment (6, two words)

indicators.note: preceding means coming before, setting the order of the two pieces

blocks.note: ne is an archaic word for not
a wage is a payment for work

explanation.surface: Ambient music was once played before the wages were handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks an old-fashioned word.
explanation.definitionFit: New Age music is the gentle, atmospheric style meant for relaxation and meditation, hence dreamy.

clue.text: Suspected terrorist, possibly, that is found clutching crumpled tenner

indicators.note: crumpled paper is creased out of shape, so the letters lose their order
clutching means holding tightly, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is
these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A suspected terrorist is caught holding a crumpled ten-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is a person detained without trial, as a suspected terrorist might be held.

clue.text: Symbol in score all over the place in operas (not old)

indicators.note: not marks something to be left out
things scattered all over the place are in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A marking in a musical score appears scattered throughout the operas.
explanation.definitionFit: A presa is the sign in a canon's score showing where each voice enters.

clue.text: Like infected blister, sore? Rule punt out

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rower with a blister wonders whether to give up punting.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is a flat-bottomed river boat pushed with a pole, a Cambridge and Oxford pastime that blisters hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Seropurulent means containing both serum and pus, which is what an infected blister holds.

clue.text: Bend in body and jerk gripping one — result of tumours

indicators.note: one thing set in another sits inside it
gripping something means holding it tightly within

blocks.note: the first letter of soma, a word for the body, which wraps round the bend
an arc is a bend or curve
the rest of soma, the body
to toss is to jerk or fling, and it wraps round the next piece
the Roman numeral for one
the last letter of toss

explanation.surface: A doctor describes a twisted body and a jerking limb as the consequence of tumours.
explanation.walkthrough: Soma is the body (as in psychosomatic); the bend goes inside it, then the jerk holds the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarcomatosis is the condition of having many sarcomas spread through the body, a state brought on by malignant tumours.

clue.text: Let's have fish, roughly a pound — what do you think?

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish, also called the orfe
the as was a Roman unit of weight of about a pound (and a coin)

explanation.surface: Someone proposes fish for dinner, about a pound of it, and asks for opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: The as was the Roman pound weight of twelve ounces, a little lighter than the modern pound, hence 'roughly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking 'Ideas?' is a casual way of inviting suggestions, the same as asking what others think.

clue.text: Nursery stuff, lush, set back round yard

indicators.note: something set back is pushed the wrong way, so its letters run in the opposite order
going round something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a lush is a drunkard, a sot
Y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: A drunk staggers back round the garden past the children's things.
explanation.definitionFit: Toys are the playthings that fill a nursery, so they are its typical contents.

clue.text: Cockney vagrant maybe left old coin

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the H sound at the start of words

blocks.note: a hobo is a tramp, one kind of vagrant
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A London tramp has left behind an ancient coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney is the working-class London accent that drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The obol was a small silver coin of ancient Greece, worth a sixth of a drachma.

clue.text: Kid lovey spoilt with ultimate in love, partner in wickedness once

indicators.note: spoilt means ruined, so the letters are knocked out of order
the ultimate of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
the final letter of love

explanation.surface: An indulged child, called lovey, turns out to be a partner in mischief.
explanation.definitionFit: A yoke-devil was an archaic term for a companion devil, a fellow in evil yoked with another.

clue.text: Fully grown as one of the best players

definitions.note: an adjective phrase via 'as': ranked as a seed

blocks.note: first meaning: having run to seed, mature
second meaning: ranked in a tournament draw among the top players

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of a mature champion; the two halves are a plant gone to seed and a player given a seeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that has seeded has reached maturity, and a seeded player is ranked among the strongest in a tournament.

clue.text: Duck and every cut requiring no preparation before cooking

indicators.note: something cut up is chopped into pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, shaped like O
these two words supply the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A duck and everything else is chopped and ready for the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a kitchen duck, but it is cricket's score of zero; 'and', usually a link, is part of the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oven-ready food has been prepared already and can go straight into the oven without further work.

clue.text: Highland cattle in the present time

blocks.note: now is the present moment
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Scottish livestock are being shown in the here and now.
explanation.walkthrough: Nowt is a Scots and northern English word for cattle (and Highland cattle are a hardy shaggy breed, which makes the surface ring true).
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect nowt means oxen or cattle, so Highland speech names the beasts this way.

clue.text: Faux pas at the bridge club? It's made by vicar all right!

definitions.text: Faux pas at the bridge club?

blocks.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title
oke is a jokey variant of OK, meaning all right

explanation.surface: A clergyman cheerfully confesses to a blunder at the card table.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, to revoke is to fail to follow suit when able to, a serious error in play.
explanation.definitionFit: A revoke is the bridge player's breach of rules by not following suit, a classic blunder at the card table.

clue.text: Buzz, possibly? A brutal nun squashes bee with one!

indicators.note: squashing crushes something out of shape, and a squashed insect is done away with, so letters are reordered and one removed

blocks.note: these letters provide the material
the spelt-out name of the letter B

explanation.surface: A violent nun swats a buzzing bee, so is the buzz just possibly hers?
explanation.walkthrough: Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon in 1969; 'Buzz' looks like the bee's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunarnaut is an astronaut who travels to the Moon, as Buzz Aldrin did with Apollo 11.

clue.text: Nominal codes unscrambled, completely grasped

indicators.note: unscrambling puts jumbled letters into a new, readable order
a thing grasped is held inside another's hold

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Cipher texts, once cracked, are fully understood in name only.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so-called is only nominally what it is labelled, existing in name rather than in fact.

clue.text: Wherein you'll see initials of Turks, usually grand royals actually

definitions.text: Wherein you'll see initials of Turks, usually grand royals actually

indicators.note: the initials of a group of words are the opening letters of each

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of these five words

explanation.surface: A description of an emblem bearing the initials of Ottoman royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a tugra (tughra) is the Ottoman sultan's calligraphic monogram, where you really do see the ruler's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The tugra was the elaborate signature-seal of an Ottoman sultan, a royal monogram stamped on decrees.

clue.text: China mug, eastern

blocks.note: a spod is a dull, swotty person, a bit of a mug
E is the abbreviation for eastern

explanation.surface: An Oriental china mug, described in a catalogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China mug' reads as one object; China is the definition and mug is a person, British slang spod meaning a nerdy bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Spode is a famous English make of porcelain, so the name stands for a kind of china.

clue.text: Most of crew in river swim brought up freshwater fish

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its last letter
in places one piece inside another
in a down clue, bringing something up reads it from the bottom upward

blocks.note: ea is an old word for a river or running water
a dip is a quick swim
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crew swimming in a river pulls up most of a catch of freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The trimmed crew goes inside the swim after the river, and the whole string is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Percidae is the family of perches, which are freshwater fish.

clue.text: Rube, dunce men ragged without hindrance

indicators.note: ragged means torn and untidy, so the letters are messed into a new order

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bumpkins and dimwits, shabbily dressed, wander about free of care.
explanation.walkthrough: A rube is an American word for a country bumpkin.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unencumbered is to be free of burdens or obstacles, which is moving without hindrance.

clue.text: Diuretic making you pee, shifting a barrier with narcotic drink (12, two words)

indicators.note: shifting things moves them about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the spelt-out name of the letter P
these letters are rearranged
ava, or kava, is a Polynesian narcotic drink

explanation.surface: A diuretic will send you to the loo, past any obstacle, with drugged drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A diuretic makes you urinate, so the surface is all of a piece with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Pareira brava is a South American root used medicinally, chiefly as a diuretic for urinary complaints.

clue.text: The old man makes something of short breaks

blocks.note: pa is a familiar word for father, one's old man
to make something of is to use it

explanation.surface: Father turns brief holidays to good account.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauses are brief stops or intervals, short breaks in activity.

clue.text: Secret remedies college fed to a prince

indicators.note: food fed to someone goes inside them

blocks.note: taken as written
a rana is a Rajput prince in India
C is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A college serves a prince confidential cures.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are secrets, and in old medicine the word meant secret remedies or elixirs.

clue.text: Rhone valley travellers may stay here — down payment required

definitions.text: Rhone valley travellers may stay here

blocks.clueFragment: Rhone valley travellers may stay here
blocks.note: first meaning: a Provençal town on the Rhône, a stop for tourists
second meaning: a Scots and northern word for earnest money paid to seal a bargain or hiring

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a hotel asking for a deposit; the place and the payment are the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a historic town on the Rhône in Provence, and arles is also old earnest money given as a pledge.

clue.text: Sycophantic one superior to maiden in cunning

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior to means placed above, setting the order of two pieces
in places the pair inside another word

blocks.note: sly means cunning
the Roman numeral for one
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A fawning suitor claims higher rank than a young woman by guile.
explanation.definitionFit: Slimy describes oily, ingratiating behaviour, which is sycophantic.

clue.text: E.g. curtain fabric, barely old but needing end trimmed

indicators.note: trimming the end of a word cuts off its final letter

blocks.note: scrimp is an obsolete adjective for scanty, barely enough

explanation.surface: Old curtain material, worn barely thin, needs its frayed edge trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old' marks the word as obsolete rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrim is a light open-weave cotton or linen used for theatre gauzes and curtains, a curtain fabric.

clue.text: Singular excrescence, malignant

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for singular
a wart is a growth on the skin, an excrescence

explanation.surface: A single growth turns out to be cancerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Swart, besides dark, can mean baleful or malignant in old poetic usage.

clue.text: One end for church: permit to deconsecrate?

indicators.note: 'end for' keeps only the last letter of 'church'

blocks.note: 'un is a dialect form of one, as in 'a good 'un'
the last letter of church
to permit is to allow

explanation.surface: A bishop's single final act for a church: permission to strip it of its sanctity.
explanation.definitionFit: To unhallow something is to remove its holiness, the reverse of consecrating, so it is a synonym of deconsecrate.

clue.text: Restless bird, kind, getting end away

indicators.note: with its end away a word loses its final letter

blocks.note: human in an old sense meant humane, kind

explanation.surface: A fidgety bird, though gentle, is finally driven off.
explanation.definitionFit: The huma is a fabulous bird of Persian legend said never to alight, so it is always restless.

clue.text: Pleasure-loving Scots, full of love, energetic

indicators.note: something full of another thing holds it inside

blocks.note: gey is the Scots form of gay in its old sense, pleasure-loving
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Fun-loving Scots, full of romance, are lively.
explanation.definitionFit: Goey means full of go, so it is a colloquial synonym of energetic.

clue.text: One paid to keen, that is in the wake of Scottish spirit

indicators.note: coming in the wake of something means following behind it, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: saul is the Scots form of soul
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A hired mourner follows a Scottish ghost at a wake.
explanation.walkthrough: A saulie is a hired mourner at a Scottish funeral; 'wake' plays on the funeral watch while meaning only 'following'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saulie was a professional mourner in Scotland, someone hired to wail, or keen, at funerals.

clue.text: Border giving Dutch trouble

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A frontier causing difficulties for the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A dado is a decorative band or border running round the lower part of a room's wall.

clue.text: Navigation system that when faulty could make marine go north

indicators.note: something faulty is broken, and broken letters re-form into something else

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A broken navigation aid could send a ship heading north by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnirange is a radio navigation system giving aircraft bearings from a beacon in any direction.

clue.text: Leader on the right board dismissed

indicators.note: what is dismissed is sent away, so those letters leave the word

blocks.note: starboard is the right-hand side of a ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chief on the right of the company board is sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a leading performer, the one who leads the cast or field.

clue.text: Date's arranged with boy's latest regular

indicators.note: arranging items puts them in a deliberately chosen new order
the latest of something is its last, here the final letter

blocks.note: these letters are rearranged
the final letter of boy

explanation.surface: A date is fixed up with a boy who becomes a regular partner.
explanation.walkthrough: A steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, as in going steady.
explanation.definitionFit: Your steady is the regular partner you date, so regular is used here as a noun.
